fasti.note: First year of the Republic (Varronian). Brutus killed in battle with Arruns Tarquinius; Collatinus forced to resign as a Tarquin. Lucretius died in office. Horatius Pulvillus dedicated the Capitoline temple (13 Sept). Polybius 3.22 dates the first treaty with Carthage to the consulship of Brutus and Horatius. The college of five is widely regarded as a later elaboration.
War with Porsenna of Clusium (Horatius Cocles, Mucius Scaevola, Cloelia in the annalistic tradition).
Some ancient authorities place the Capitoline dedication in this year.
Aristodemus of Cumae and the Latins defeat Arruns Porsenna at Aricia (Greek-based date c. 504).
Migration of Attus Clausus (Appius Claudius) and his Sabine following to Rome.
Livy reports the first dictatorship (Titus Larcius) in this year or 498; the sources disagree.
Praenomen of Veturius given as Publius in some sources. Livy dates Lake Regillus here, Dionysius in 496.
Temple of Saturn dedicated (Livy 2.21).
Battle of Lake Regillus against the Latins, conventionally dated here; Postumius as dictator vowed the temple of Castor.
Death of Tarquinius Superbus at Cumae. Temple of Mercury dedicated. Debt crisis.
First secession of the plebs (to the Mons Sacer or Aventine); tribunes of the plebs created (traditionally 494/493). Manius Valerius dictator.
Foedus Cassianum with the Latins. Temple of Ceres, Liber and Libera vowed (dedicated this year per Dionysius). Capture of Corioli attributed to Gnaeus Marcius (Coriolanus).
Famine; grain bought in Etruria and Sicily.
Trial and exile of Coriolanus in the annalistic tradition.
Coriolanus and the Volsci before Rome (488 in Livy). Furius' cognomen uncertain (Medullinus Fusus?).
Cognomina (Sabinus, Tuscus) are late and doubtful.
Treaty with the Hernici. Cassius proposes an agrarian law; executed 485 for aiming at kingship (adfectatio regni).
First of seven successive years with a Fabius as consul (485-479).
Temple of Castor dedicated (15 July).
Vestal Oppia buried alive.
Battle against Veii; Manlius and Quintus Fabius (cos. 485) killed.
The Fabii take up the war with Veii privately and fortify a post on the Cremera.
Servilius died in office.
Destruction of the 306 Fabii on the Cremera (Ovid, Fasti 2.193-196, gives 13 February; Livy and others assimilate it to the dies Alliensis, 18 July). Menenius later prosecuted.
Veientines occupy the Janiculum.
Forty-year truce with Veii. Hiero of Syracuse defeats the Etruscans off Cumae (synchronism).
Murder of the tribune Gnaeus Genucius.
Lex Publilia Voleronis: tribunes elected by an assembly voting by tribes (concilium plebis tributum).
Antium taken from the Volsci; colony at Antium 467.
Pestilence; both consuls die (Livy 3.6-7).
Tribune Gaius Terentilius Harsa proposes a commission to codify the law.
Trial of Caeso Quinctius, son of Cincinnatus.
Appius Herdonius seizes the Capitol with exiles and slaves; Valerius killed retaking it, replaced by Cincinnatus.
Minucius trapped by the Aequi on Mount Algidus; Cincinnatus named dictator from his plough, relieves him and resigns after sixteen days (Livy 3.26-29).
Tribunes of the plebs raised to ten.
Lex Icilia de Aventino publicando: the Aventine assigned to the plebs.
Lex Aternia Tarpeia on fines (in cattle and sheep). Embassy to Athens to study Solon's laws (traditional).
Quinctilius died of plague.
Embassy returns from Greece.
The consuls elect abdicated in favour of the first decemvirate (decemviri legibus scribundis), listed under 'tribunes'. Ten tables of law published.
Second decemvirate (half plebeian in Livy's list). Two further tables, including the ban on patrician-plebeian intermarriage. The 'tyranny' of Appius and the Verginia story belong to 450-449.

Fall of the decemvirs after the death of Verginia; second secession of the plebs. Leges Valeriae Horatiae: plebiscites binding (doubted as anachronistic), right of provocatio, sacrosanctity of tribunes reaffirmed. The decemvirs held office into this year.
Quaestors first elected by the people (Tacitus, Ann. 11.22).
Dispute of Ardea and Aricia over Corioli land awarded by the Roman people to itself.
Lex Canuleia permits intermarriage (conubium) between patricians and plebeians. Consular tribunate created as a compromise (Livy 4.1-6).

First consular tribunes; they abdicated after three months as vitio creati and were replaced by suffect consuls. The suffects are known from Licinius Macer's linen books (libri lintei) and are absent from some lists.
Censorship created; first censors Lucius Papirius Mugillanus and Lucius Sempronius Atratinus.
Colony at Ardea.
Famine; Lucius Minucius appointed praefectus annonae.
Spurius Maelius, a rich plebeian distributing grain, killed by Gaius Servilius Ahala, master of horse to the dictator Cincinnatus.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Fidenae defects to Lars Tolumnius of Veii; Roman envoys murdered.
Aulus Cornelius Cossus kills Lars Tolumnius and wins the spolia opima; Livy (4.20) notes Augustus' claim that Cossus' linen corslet named him consul, i.e. 428.
Pestilence. Villa Publica built in the Campus Martius by the censors.
Livy (4.23) records that Licinius Macer and Valerius Antias gave these consuls, while Aelius Tubero gave consular tribunes. Lex Aemilia limits the censorship to 18 months.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Plague; temple to Apollo Medicus vowed.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. First law on electoral canvassing (white toga) attributed to this year.
Dictator Aulus Postumius Tubertus defeats Aequi and Volsci on Mount Algidus. Temple of Apollo dedicated by Julius.
Livy names Papirius Crassus and Julius; Diodorus differs. Lex Iulia Papiria commutes fines into bronze.
Year Augustus claimed for Cossus' spolia opima.
Declaration of war on Veii voted by the comitia centuriata.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Mamercus Aemilius dictator captures and destroys Fidenae.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Twenty-year truce with Veii (or eight years per some accounts).

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Samnites seize Capua (Livy 4.37; Diodorus 423).
Sempronius' defeat by the Volsci; later prosecuted.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges.
Quaestors increased from two to four and opened to plebeians. Samnites take Cumae (Diodorus).

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Vestal Postumia tried and acquitted.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Slave conspiracy suppressed.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Labici taken.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Colony at Labici (1,500 settlers, 2 iugera each).

Postumius stoned to death by his own troops after refusing them the plunder of Bolae.
Pestilence and famine; grain from Etruria and Sicily.
Arx Carventana lost and recovered.
First plebeian quaestors elected.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Verrugo lost to the Volsci.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Anxur (Tarracina) captured. Pay (stipendium) for soldiers introduced, funded by tributum (Livy 4.59-60). War with Veii declared.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Siege of Veii begins (traditionally ten years, 405-396, an assimilation to Troy).

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Colony sent to Velitrae.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Livy (5.1) gives eight names, apparently including the two censors (Marcus Furius Camillus and Marcus Postumius); the list here omits Camillus as censor. Winter siege at Veii first maintained.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Quarrel of Verginius and Sergius at Veii leads to a defeat; both forced to resign.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Camillus' first consular tribunate.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Licinius Calvus the first plebeian consular tribune in Livy's account (5.12); some names in earlier colleges may also be plebeian.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Majority plebeian college. First lectisternium, on Sibylline advice.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Alban Lake overflows; Delphi consulted.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Draining tunnel (emissarium) of the Alban Lake associated with this prodigy.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Camillus, dictator, takes Veii; Juno Regina evoked to Rome (temple on the Aventine 392). The Licinius of this year is the son of the tribune of 400. Ager Veientanus annexed, nearly doubling Roman territory.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Proposal to migrate half the population to Veii rejected.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Falerii surrenders (the schoolmaster story). Gold bowl sent to Delphi as a tithe of Veii's spoil.
Livy (5.29) records the first pair as elected but has the second pair as suffects (or as consuls of 392 in some lists); the arrangement of 393-392 is confused in the sources.
Livy places Valerius and Manlius here; temple of Juno Regina dedicated on the Aventine.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Camillus exiled to Ardea (Livy) after a prosecution over the Veii booty.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Gallic sack of Rome after the Allia (18 July, dies Alliensis). Varronian 390 corresponds to Greek-synchronised 387/386 (Polybius 1.6). Brennus and the ransom of 1,000 pounds of gold; the tale of Camillus' rescue is apologetic fiction.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Camillus dictator defeats the Volsci at Mecium. Records said to have been destroyed in the sack (Livy 6.1), a claim modern scholars treat with reserve.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Four new tribes on the ager Veientanus (Stellatina, Tromentina, Sabatina, Arnensis): 25 tribes.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Satricum recovered; Latin colonies at Sutrium and Nepet (383 per Velleius).

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Aulus Cornelius Cossus dictator; Marcus Manlius Capitolinus imprisoned for agitation over debt. Colony at Satricum.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Marcus Manlius Capitolinus condemned for aiming at kingship and thrown from the Tarpeian Rock.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Colony at Nepet (Livy) or Sutrium.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. War with Velitrae and Praeneste.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Tusculum incorporated with Roman citizenship, the first municipium (traditional).

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Livy (6.27) gives a longer college of which only some names are secure; this list is partial and its composition uncertain. Titus Quinctius Cincinnatus dictator defeats Praeneste on the Allia and dedicates a statue of Jupiter Imperator.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Eight names in Livy (6.30), five of them plebeian.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Censors let the contract for a wall of squared stone (Livy 6.32); the surviving 'Servian' wall in Grotta Oscura tufa is generally dated after the Gallic sack.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Battle at Satricum against Latins and Volsci.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Gaius Licinius Stolo and Lucius Sextius Lateranus elected tribunes of the plebs and propose their laws.

'Anarchy' (solitudo magistratuum): Livy (6.35) says Licinius and Sextius vetoed all curule elections for five years (375-371). Diodorus has only one year without magistrates. The five-year figure is probably an artefact of the Varronian chronology, which had to fill a gap relative to Greek synchronisms.
Anarchy, second year (Livy's five-year version).
Anarchy, third year (Livy's five-year version).
Anarchy, fourth year (Livy's five-year version).
Anarchy, fifth year (Livy's five-year version).

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Velitrae besieged.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Camillus dictator (IV) resigns; Publius Manlius dictator names a plebeian, Gaius Licinius, master of horse. Keepers of the Sibylline books raised to ten (decemviri sacris faciundis), half plebeian.

Consular tribunes (tribuni militum consulari potestate) in place of consuls. Names follow Livy and Broughton, MRR I; Livy, Diodorus and the Fasti Capitolini differ in number, order and identity for many of these colleges. Last consular tribunes. Leges Liciniae Sextiae: one consul may (or must) be plebeian; limit of 500 iugera on ager publicus (the figure possibly retrojected from the second century); debt relief. Camillus dictator (V) vows the temple of Concord.
Sextius the first plebeian consul. Praetorship created (first praetor Spurius Furius Camillus) and curule aedileship; ludi Romani extended by a day.
Pestilence; death of Camillus.
Ludi scaenici introduced with Etruscan performers to appease the gods during the plague (Livy 7.2). Some sources make the plebeian consul Gaius Licinius Stolo himself.
Lucius Manlius Capitolinus Imperiosus dictator clavi figendi causa; Marcus Curtius' leap into the chasm in the Forum (one version).
Genucius, the first plebeian consul to command an army under his own auspices, killed fighting the Hernici. Six military tribunes now elected by the people.
Titus Manlius wins the cognomen Torquatus by killing a Gallic champion at the Anio (Claudius Quadrigarius in Gellius 9.13; Livy dates the fight here).
Gauls near Rome; Gaius Poetelius triumphs over Gauls and Tiburtines.
Tribes Pomptina and Publilia created (27 tribes). Lex Poetelia de ambitu. Treaty with the Latins renewed.
Lex Manlia imposes a 5% tax on manumissions, passed by the army in camp at Sutrium. Lex Duilia Menenia caps interest at one-twelfth (unciarium faenus).
Gaius Marcius Rutilus the first plebeian dictator.
Two patrician consuls, in breach of the Licinian law; repeated in several years 355-343.
Treaty with the Samnites (Livy 7.19; Diodorus 16.45).
Caere granted a hundred-year truce.
Quinqueviri mensarii appointed to liquidate debts.
Gaius Marcius Rutilus the first plebeian censor.
Popillius defeats a Gallic army in Latium.
Claudius died before taking the field; Camillus sole consul. Marcus Valerius wins the cognomen Corvus in single combat with a Gaul aided by a raven.
Treaty with Carthage (Livy 7.27, Diodorus 16.69); probably the 'second treaty' of Polybius 3.24.
Interest reduced to one twenty-fourth (semunciarium) and debts rescheduled. Plautius' cognomen given as Hypsaeus or Venox.
Satricum destroyed.
Sora taken from the Volsci. Temple of Juno Moneta vowed (dedicated 344).
Temple of Juno Moneta dedicated on the Arx.
First Samnite War (343-341) after Capua's deditio. Battles of Mount Gaurus, Saticula and Suessula. Historicity of the war is debated; Carthage sends a gold crown.
Mutiny of the garrison in Campania. Leges Genuciae: ban on lending at interest; no one to hold the same magistracy within ten years; both consuls may be plebeian.
Peace with the Samnites; revolt of the Latins begins.
Latin War. Battle near Vesuvius (Veseris): Decius' devotio; Torquatus executes his son for fighting a duel against orders. Trifanum.
Leges Publiliae (Philo as dictator): plebiscites binding on all; patrum auctoritas given in advance for centuriate laws; one censor must be plebeian.

Latin settlement: League dissolved; some cities incorporated as municipia (Lanuvium, Aricia, Nomentum, Pedum), others with civitas sine suffragio (Capua, Fundi, Formiae, Cumae). Beaks of Antiate ships fixed to the speakers' platform (Rostra); column of Maenius.
Quintus Publilius Philo the first plebeian praetor.
Cales captured.
Latin colony of 2,500 at Cales. Postumius later called Caudinus. Alexander of Epirus campaigning in southern Italy; supposed treaty with Rome.

Dictator year: no consuls. The Fasti Capitolini insert a year in which a dictator (Publius Cornelius Rufinus, with master of horse Marcus Antonius) held office without consuls. Livy and the other literary sources ignore these four years (333, 324, 309, 301); they are a late-Republican chronographic device (associated with Atticus and Varro) to reconcile Roman and Greek chronology.
Tribes Maecia and Scaptia created (29). Treaty with Alexander of Epirus (Livy 8.17).
Poisoning scandal: 170 matronae condemned (Livy 8.18); dictator clavi figendi causa. Valerius' cognomen given as Flaccus or Potitus.
War with Privernum and Fundi.
Privernum taken. Colony at Tarracina (Anxur), citizen colony of 300.
Latin colony at Fregellae on the Liris, provoking the Samnites. Some lists have Gaius Plautius Decianus II.
War with Neapolis (Palaeopolis).
Philo's command prorogued: the first promagistracy. Neapolis becomes an ally (foedus aequum). Second Samnite War begins. Lex Poetelia Papiria abolishes nexum (debt bondage); Varro dates it to 313.
Vestini join the Samnites. Papirius Cursor dictator clashes with his master of horse Quintus Fabius Rullianus, who fought against orders.
Dictator year: Lucius Papirius Cursor continues as dictator without consuls (Fasti Capitolini only; ignored by Livy). See 333 BC.
Apulians allied.
Fulvius, from Tusculum, consul in the same year he was a magistrate there (Pliny NH 7.136).
Caudine Forks: both consuls' armies trapped by Gavius Pontius and sent under the yoke; the sponsio disowned by the Senate. Fregellae lost.
Livy's story of revenge at Luceria and Caudium in 320-319 is regarded as invented; the Romans more probably observed the Caudine peace until 316.
Some lists have Lucius Papirius Mugillanus instead of Cursor.
Tribes Oufentina and Falerna created (31). Praefecti sent to Capua. Two-year truce with the Samnites.
Apulia brought over; Teanum Apulum and Canusium.
War with the Samnites renewed; Lucius Aemilius dictator at Saticula.
Roman defeat at Lautulae (Fabius Rullianus dictator); Capua wavers. Saticula and Luceria taken.
Samnites defeated near Tarracina; Latin colony at Luceria (2,500). Campanian conspiracy suppressed.
Colonies at Suessa Aurunca, Pontiae, Saticula; Nola, Atina, Calatia captured.

Censorship of Appius Claudius Caecus (with Gaius Plautius): Via Appia to Capua and the Aqua Appia, Rome's first aqueduct; humiliores distributed through all tribes; freedmen's sons admitted to the Senate. Livy gives Valerius as Maximus.
Duoviri navales first elected; sixteen of the military tribunes elected by the people. Etruscan cities attack Sutrium. Temple of Salus vowed.
Fabius crosses the Ciminian Forest into Etruria and defeats the Etruscans near Perusia. Marcius (later Censorinus) wounded in Samnium.
Dictator year: Lucius Papirius Cursor dictator, said to have defeated the Samnites at Longula, without consuls (Fasti Capitolini only). See 333 BC.
Peace or truce with Tarquinii (40 years); Nuceria Alfaterna defects.
Agathocles-period treaty contacts. Volumnius campaigns among the Sallentini.

Revolt and defeat of the Hernici; Anagnia given civitas sine suffragio. Treaty renewed with Carthage (Livy 9.43), perhaps the 'Philinus treaty' denied by Polybius. Equestrian statue of Marcius in the Forum.
Bovianum captured; Minucius killed (or mortally wounded) and replaced by Fulvius.

Peace with the Samnites ends the Second Samnite War. Aequi crushed. Gnaeus Flavius, curule aedile and son of a freedman, publishes the legis actiones and the calendar; dedicates a shrine of Concord. Censors Quintus Fabius and Publius Decius confine the humiles to the four urban tribes; transvectio equitum instituted (15 July).
Latin colonies at Alba Fucens (6,000) and Sora (4,000). Arpinum and Trebula given civitas sine suffragio.

Cleonymus of Sparta raids the Italian coast; temple of Salus dedicated by Gaius Junius Bubulcus, with paintings by Fabius Pictor (the first Roman painter of note). Treaty with Tarentum barring Roman ships beyond the Lacinian promontory may belong here.

Dictator year: Marcus Valerius Corvus dictator without consuls (Fasti Capitolini only). Livy (10.3-5) has a dictatorship this year for war in Etruria (Arretium) and against the Marsi but treats it within a consular year. See 333 BC.
